title: Defensive semantic versioning, LTS channels, and rollout guardrails for serving runtime
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define a defensive semantic versioning policy and operational rollout guardrails for the serving runtime that balance the need for evolution with customer stability. Deliverables: a single-page policy doc for maintainers, a deprecation schedule matrix, LTS channel semantics, automated pre-release compatibility checks, and a minimal 'migration assistant' CLI that generates shims or client guidance when breaking changes are unavoidable. This ticket codifies categories of breaking changes, deprecation windows by impact tier, canary + progressive rollout gates, telemetry signals for safe promotion, and the integration points for release tooling (amcli/upgrade-tooling).
acceptance_criteria: A concise semver policy page (1-2 pages) that defines major/minor/patch semantics for runtime public contracts and clearly lists 'allowed internal changes' vs 'user-impacting changes'

Deprecation matrix published: impact tiers (non-breaking, opt-in change, soft-deprecation, hard-deprecation) with concrete timelines (90/180/365 days) and required notices (release notes + response headers)
LTS channel behavior documented: guaranteed security/patch support window, backported fixes policy, and compatibility promise for third-party SDKs
Rollout gate checklist implemented as an automated CI job that runs compatibility test battery and emits a promote/hold signal
A minimal migration assistant (amcli mig-check) that can run against a customer config to surface required client-side changes and optionally generate shim code examples
Telemetry gates configured: error-rate thresholds, latency regressions, and model-output-quality regressions mapped to automatic rollback criteria
Runbook for upgrade failures documented with clear owner, rollback steps, and postmortem template
steps: Draft policy wording and internal FAQ; review with infra, SDK, and product teams
Enumerate public runtime API surfaces (gRPC, REST, headers, payload schemas) and map compatibility expectations
Define deprecation headers and notice URIs for our API responses
Implement CI compatibility suite (contract tests + e2e smoke) and add promote/hold signal in release pipeline
Prototype 'migration assistant' CLI that inspects client usage patterns and suggests shims or config changes
Design LTS channel metadata and publishable tags; create process to nominate a release for LTS
Create telemetry dashboards and SLO-based promotion thresholds for canaries
Document rollback circuit and emergency compatibility fallback flow (model-variant routing, API adapter toggles)
notes: Decision: Use a conservative semver interpretation where 'major' increments require explicit migration guides and a deprecation window unless the change fixes a critical security issue.
Trade-off: Longer deprecation windows slow UX for iterative improvements; mitigations include offering experimental flags and opt-in minor-version features.
Compatibility shim approach: prefer server-side shims for common client migrations to minimize customer churn, but provide client code snippets and SDK helpers for complex schema changes.
Backport policy: LTS releases will receive critical and security fixes only; functional changes go to minor releases.
We will introduce a 'compatibility-intent' release header in pre-release builds to help client SDKs opt-in to new behavior during canaries.
Plan to iterate on thresholds for telemetry gates during the first 3 minor releases after runtime-2.0 to calibrate sensitivity.
Risk: Generating shims for every breaking change is not scalable; we will prioritize shims for high-usage SDKs and common call patterns based on telemetry.
Follow-up: run a 1-week tabletop exercise simulating a major breaking change to validate rollout and rollback playbooks.
